item_description: A very large tortoise native to the Aldabra Atoll in the Seychelles, where it feeds on vegetation.
item_facts: It is among the largest living tortoises.
It can live for many decades, with some individuals exceeding a century.
It shapes its island habitat by browsing plants and dispersing seeds.
needs_review: Size, longevity and ecosystem claims not externally verified.

item_description: A large crocodilian native to the southeastern United States, commonly found in freshwater wetlands.
item_facts: It is one of two living alligator species; the other is the Chinese alligator.
It creates depressions called alligator holes that can retain water during dry periods.
Its sex is influenced by incubation temperature in the nest.
needs_review: Range, ecosystem role and temperature-dependent sex claims not externally verified.

item_description: A long, highly venomous African snake whose dark mouth interior gives it its common name.
item_facts: Its body is typically gray, olive or brown rather than black.
It is native to sub-Saharan Africa.
It hunts small mammals and birds.
needs_review: Appearance, range and diet claims not externally verified.

item_description: A group of crocodilian reptiles native to Central and South America, usually associated with rivers and wetlands.
item_facts: Caimans belong to the alligator family, Alligatoridae.
Their diet changes with species and age and can include fish and invertebrates.
Several caiman species inhabit freshwater wetlands and waterways.
needs_review: Common name covers multiple species; verify species scope, diet and range.

item_description: An Australian and New Guinean lizard known for the large skin frill it spreads when threatened.
item_facts: The frill is supported by cartilage attached to the jaw and hyoid region.
It is primarily arboreal and often climbs trees to forage.
When alarmed, it may run bipedally toward cover.
needs_review: Anatomy, habitat and behavior claims not externally verified.

item_description: A heavy-bodied African viper with elaborate leaf-like markings and very long fangs.
item_facts: It has among the longest fangs of any venomous snake.
Its camouflage helps it blend into leaf litter.
It is an ambush predator that can remain still for extended periods.
needs_review: Anatomy and behavior claims not externally verified.

item_description: A stocky, venomous lizard of the southwestern United States and northwestern Mexico, patterned in black and orange or pink.
item_facts: It is one of only two venomous lizard species, the other being the beaded lizard.
It stores fat in its tail, which helps it survive periods without food.
It uses its forked tongue to collect scent particles while tracking prey.

source_refs.title: Gila Monster, San Diego Zoo Wildlife Alliance

item_description: A large South American boa that lives in wetlands and waterways and subdues prey by constriction.
item_facts: It is the heaviest snake species, while the reticulated python can reach greater lengths.
Females are much larger than males.
It gives birth to live young rather than laying eggs.

item_description: A large herbivorous lizard native to Central and South America and several Caribbean islands.
item_facts: It is an excellent climber and often lives in trees near water.
A crest of spines runs along its back and tail.
It can drop its tail to escape a predator and later regrow a shorter one.
needs_review: Range, habitat and tail-regeneration claims not externally verified.

item_description: A large nonvenomous python of South Asia that kills prey by constriction.
item_facts: It is also known as the Indian rock python.
Its diet includes mammals and birds.
Females lay eggs and may coil around them while they incubate.
needs_review: Taxonomy, range and reproductive details not externally verified.

item_description: An elusive, highly venomous snake native to arid inland areas of Australia.
item_facts: It is also called the western taipan or fierce snake.
Its natural prey consists mainly of small mammals.
It usually inhabits cracking-clay soils and other dry inland environments.
needs_review: Common names, diet and habitat details not externally verified.

item_description: A large venomous Asian snake that can raise the front of its body and spread a hood when threatened.
item_facts: It is the only living species in the genus Ophiophagus.
It feeds mainly on other snakes.
A female builds a nest for her eggs, a rare behavior among snakes.
needs_review: Taxonomy, diet and nesting behavior not externally verified.

item_description: The largest living lizard, native to a small group of Indonesian islands.
item_facts: It is a monitor lizard with a muscular tail and powerful claws.
Adult Komodo dragons hunt and scavenge animals including deer and wild pigs.
Young Komodo dragons spend time in trees, where they are less vulnerable to larger dragons.

source_refs.title: Komodo Dragon, San Diego Zoo Wildlife Alliance

item_description: The largest living turtle, a wide-ranging marine reptile with a flexible, leathery shell rather than a hard scuted shell.
item_facts: It migrates across ocean basins between feeding and nesting areas.
Jellyfish are a major part of its diet.
Its shell is supported by a mosaic of small bones beneath a leathery skin.
needs_review: Size, migration, diet and shell anatomy claims not externally verified.

item_description: A freshwater turtle of South American rivers, known for a flattened, leaf-like head and rough shell.
item_facts: It is an ambush predator that often remains motionless on the river bottom.
Its unusual head shape helps it blend into leaf litter and aquatic vegetation.
It captures prey by rapidly opening its mouth and drawing in water.
needs_review: Species behavior, anatomy and range not externally verified.

item_description: A large African crocodile found in freshwater habitats and some brackish waters.
item_facts: It is an ambush predator that can remain nearly motionless at the water's edge.
Its diet ranges from fish to large mammals, depending on the crocodile's size.
Nile crocodiles guard nests and may carry hatchlings to water.
needs_review: Range, prey and parental care claims not externally verified.

item_description: A large semi-aquatic monitor lizard native to much of sub-Saharan Africa.
item_facts: It is a strong swimmer and often lives near rivers and wetlands.
Its diet includes eggs, fish, crustaceans, birds and small mammals.
It uses a long, forked tongue to sample chemical cues in its environment.
needs_review: Species distribution, diet and sensory claims not externally verified.

item_description: A nonvenomous Southeast Asian python with a net-like pattern and exceptional potential length.
item_facts: It is widely regarded as the longest snake species, though the largest verified specimens are uncommon.
It kills prey by constriction.
It is an adept swimmer and occurs on islands as well as mainland areas.
needs_review: Length ranking, distribution and swimming claims not externally verified.

item_description: The largest living reptile, found in coastal and freshwater habitats across parts of South and Southeast Asia and Australia.
item_facts: It can travel through seawater between coastal areas.
It is an ambush predator with a varied diet that changes as it grows.
Males may defend territories in estuaries and river systems.
needs_review: Size ranking, range and behavior claims not externally verified.

item_description: A small Australian desert lizard covered in conical spines that help deter predators and break up its outline.
item_facts: It feeds mainly on ants.
Tiny channels between its scales can direct water toward its mouth.
It can change color in response to temperature and activity.
needs_review: Species-specific diet, water transport and color-change claims not externally verified.
